title: Inconsistency between Frequentist and Bayesian inference, approximation of improper priors and permissible priors
summary: Improper priors are widely used in objective Bayesian inference, although posterior propriety does not by itself guarantee coherence between Bayesian and frequentist assessments. We investigate this issue by approximating improper priors with proper priors and examining the convergence of the resulting posterior distributions. We introduce monotone $q$-vague convergence, which ensures pointwise Kullback-Leibler (KL) convergence of the posteriors, and study expected KL (EKL) convergence together with its total variation counterpart (ETV).
